req.title: Update existing post
req.statement: The system shall update the row when POST /<id>/update is called by the post's author with a title and body, and redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update by the post's author with a valid title and body must update the DB row and return a 302 redirect to /. I designed: (1) a positive EP test confirming the happy path — correct author, valid title+body → 302 to /, DB row updated; (2) a negative NEG test where a non-author (user 'other') attempts to update user 1's post → 403; (3) a boundary BVA test where title is an empty string → no redirect, error message shown (title required); (4) a DT test where an unauthenticated client hits the endpoint → 302 to /auth/login; (5) a STC test verifying the DB state transition: title and body values are exactly the new values after update, not the old ones. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_update_post_by_author_redirects_and_persists
preconditions: DB seeded with user id=1 (test/test) and post id=1 authored by user 1
actions: POST /1/update with title='updated title', body='updated body'
expected: DB row for post id=1 has title='updated title' and body='updated body'
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})

r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'updated title', 'body': 'updated body'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f"Expected '/', got {r.headers['Location']}"

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert row['title'] == 'updated title', f"title mismatch: {row['title']}"
    assert row['body'] == 'updated body', f"body mismatch: {row['body']}"

def test_update_post_by_author_redirects_and_persists():

tests.name: test_update_post_db_state_transition_exact_values
preconditions: DB seeded: post id=1 has title='test title', body='test\nbody'
actions: POST /1/update with title='new title', body='new body'
Query DB for post id=1 title and body
expected: After update: title == 'new title' exactly, body == 'new body' exactly
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    before = db.execute('SELECT title, body, author_id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert before['title'] == 'test title'
    assert before['body'] == 'test\nbody'
    assert before['author_id'] == 1

client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'new title', 'body': 'new body'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    after = db.execute('SELECT title, body, author_id FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
    assert after['title'] == 'new title', f"Expected 'new title', got {after['title']}"
    assert after['body'] == 'new body', f"Expected 'new body', got {after['body']}"
    assert after['author_id'] == 1, f"author_id mutated: {after['author_id']}"

def test_update_post_db_state_transition_exact_values():
    pass
